why: Both moved the same single call identically and both found the prompt-cache bug, but A's versions are consistently the more expert ones: it splits only the volatile {date}/{time} lines out instead of shoving the whole system prompt behind the history, it verified cross-vendor fallback end-to-end through on_message (including the image path and the served tier, the very Flex interaction B flagged as unmeasured), and it actually measured the app's biggest lever — a 148x cheaper default on sampled real prompts — instead of leaving it as an open question. B's edge is one genuine product fix A missed entirely (telling the user when a generation fails) plus sharper fidelity notes, but its built work is coarser and its strongest proposals are unmeasured.
A_best: i4: measured, live, side-by-side that gpt-6-luna at effort low answers this bot's prompts for 1/148th of gpt-5.5's cost at comparable latency, with :vision kept for the image path and gpt-5.5 one /model away — the right question (should this call use a frontier model at all?) asked and answered with evidence rather than deferred.
B_best: i3: making failures visible in Discord instead of a stopped typing indicator, correctly argued as newly urgent on Router (spend cap 401, credits 402, 429, 504 all land in the same swallowed except) and implemented safely inside its own try/except without touching msg_nodes bookkeeping.
A_worst: It never fixed the bare `except Exception: logging.exception` — after fallbacks exhaust, a user still gets silence with no signal — and its one needs-decision (unlocking api.x.ai for grok) is near-worthless since config.yaml ships no x-ai model.
B_worst: The two highest-value system judgments are left unmeasured decisions (d2 only suggests gpt-5.4/5.4-mini, never finding the sub-dollar tier; d1 admits it never measured which tier serves a fallback list), and its cache fix relocates the entire system prompt behind 25 messages of history when only the clock lines needed to move.
